## A sharp linear bounded-error exponent with a bounded reference

Assume |z|<=rmax<1, reference amplitudes R<=Rmax, and physical raw intensity
I=|h+R exp(i theta)|^2/2. For unit v and 0<epsilon<=1 choose S0=s=0,
t=sqrt(epsilon)v. This reciprocal source is passive; ||G||=epsilon and
h=z epsilon(v^T u)^2. Relative to the zero source, for every unit/subunit u,
load and reference phase,

    |I-I_zero| <= Rmax rmax epsilon+rmax^2 epsilon^2/2
                 <= C epsilon,
    C=Rmax rmax+rmax^2/2.

For C>0 and 0<delta<=C set epsilon=delta/C. The zero-source transcript is
compatible with both sources under raw errors bounded by delta, regardless
of the number of adaptive queries. Every Gram estimator has worst-case error
at least delta/(2C) on one source. For deterministic control in dimension>=2,
choose v bilinearly orthogonal to the returned command on the common
transcript; its regret is delta/C.

This matches the new linear exponent, up to constants/dimension, for bounded
reference power. It neither changes the original intensity-only square-root
theorem nor supplies a photon lower bound. Unbounded free reference power is
outside this contract; calibration, dynamic range and photons remain charged.

## 10. Matching bounded-error exponent for a bounded reference

The linear precision exponent is sharp under fixed bounded reference amplitude. This is another bounded-error indistinguishability statement, not a photon lower bound. Suppose every allowed reference has `R<=Rmax`. For `0<eta<=Rmax+1/2`, put `tau=eta/(Rmax+1/2)<=1` and compare the zero source with the reciprocal passive source `S0=s=0`, `t=sqrt(tau) v`, where `v` is unit. Every unit/subunit input and passive load gives `|h_z(u)|<=tau`. Consequently

\[
\left|\tfrac12|h_z+R e^{i\theta}|^2-\tfrac12R^2\right|
\le R_{max}\tau+\tfrac12\tau^2
\le(R_{max}+\tfrac12)\tau=\eta.
\]

The zero-source transcript is admissible for both sources under simultaneous raw error `eta`, regardless of the number of adaptive settings. Their target Grams differ by norm `tau`, so every estimator has worst-case error at least `eta/[2(Rmax+1/2)]` on one source. For deterministic control in dimension at least two, choose `v` bilinearly orthogonal to the output command on that transcript; regret is `tau`. Thus uniform linear error scaling cannot be surpassed at fixed bounded reference. Permitting an unbounded uncharged reference under a fixed absolute detector-error oracle would change the metrology problem again.

## E. Exact information failures and bounded-reference exponent

The two scalar passive matrices in NEW_LIMITS have equal returns 0 and1/32
at loads0,1/2 but target powers1/16 and1/25; their -1/2 returns differ.
Symmetric row-sum bounds certify contraction. Scaling t'=ct,s'=c^2s and
z'=z/c^2 preserves every complex return while p'=c^2p whenever passivity
survives. The explicit rational scale witness remains passive. Neither full
coherent access nor adaptive commands removes an unacquired load scale.

For A=1/10,k=1/5, A(1+ikz)/(1-ikz) equals a false target with residue2ikA
and pole ik. Its phase factors at+-1/2 are (99+-20i)/101. A load-dependent
reference rotation of a target-free constant A therefore produces all twelve
false-source powers exactly. Choose t with t^2=2ikA; |t|=1/5 and symmetric
row sums<=2/5 show the false two-port is passive. A fit cannot acquire reference
commonality. The separate load-dependent gain failure is not automatically
indistinguishable in all reference sums.

For bounded R<=Rmax and |z|<=rmax<1, a source with t=sqrt(epsilon)v and
S0=s=0 is passive, ||G||=epsilon, and |h|<=rmax epsilon. Every intensity differs
from its zero-source value by at most C epsilon,
C=Rmax rmax+rmax^2/2. For 0<delta<=C, take epsilon=delta/C. One common
transcript gives worst-case Gram error at least delta/(2C). For deterministic
control,n>=2, a unit v bilinearly orthogonal to the transcript's command gives
regret epsilon. This matches a linear bounded-error exponent at fixed bounded
reference, not optimal dimension constants or a photon lower bound. The
coherent note's looser rmax=1 constant is consistent with NEW_LIMITS.
